newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Feb 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Feb 17.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
- China reports record $10 billion in foreign currency from tourism in 1996
- The State Statistical Bureau announced that the number of school dropouts aged 6 to 14 was down 14.51 million in 1995, or 10 percent lower than 1990.
- Over the new year, the documentary on Deng Xiaoping was hailed by many Tibetans
- The State Council issued a circular calling on transport departments to do better job in helping migrant workers return to their designations to work.
- Wu Wenying, president of the China National Textiles Council, said her council will accelerate pace of reform and make textile industry more competitive on the market.
- China tightens grip on state assets in joint stock companies and Sino-foreign joint ventures
- Central bank's Shanghai branch to adopt supervision methods used by World Bank
- Shenzhen Urban Cooperative Bank profits hit 370 million yuan in 1996, exceeding target by 152.7 percent
- An opinion poll shows most Chinese youth say they will not forget the history of Japan's invasion of China.
- China's wool imports are expected to continue to decline.
